question.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)
$$

The Fourier series of the $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-2, & x\in [0,\pi ) \\ 3, & x\in [-\pi ,0)\end{aligned}
$$

is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{4}.$

${a}_{4}=$ {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the cosine coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=\pi .$ Also, $f(x)=-2$ for $x\in [0,\pi )$ and $f(x)=3$ for $x\in [-\pi ,0).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{4} & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{0}3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(-2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{4}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)]}_{-\pi }^{0}-\frac{2}{\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{4}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{3}{4\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-4\pi ))-\frac{1}{2\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
